lead: Huntsville is one of the fastest-growing cities in the South, with many newer homes. Flash flooding, storm damage and crawl space moisture drive most of its water damage.
risk: flash flooding, storm damage and crawl space moisture
why: Huntsville sits in a valley ringed by hills and mountains, including Monte Sano to the east. Heavy rain runs off the slopes fast and fills creeks like Pinhook, Aldridge and Indian Creek. Low streets and homes near those creeks can flood within an hour. Many Huntsville homes sit over crawl spaces, and in a humid Alabama summer, a small leak there can lead to rot and mold.

Severe storms are the other big risk. On April 27, 2011, a historic tornado outbreak tore across north Alabama. Tornadoes hit parts of Madison County, and power was out across Huntsville for days. Spring storms still drop trees and peel back shingles most years. Much of the city's housing was built after 1980, so many roofs and water heaters are reaching the end of their life.
image_alt: Roofer working on new roof framing
image_caption: Storm-damaged Huntsville roofs often need new framing and decking.
problems: Homes near Pinhook and Aldridge creeks
Wooded areas like Blossomwood, Jones Valley
Crawl space drying and mold control
tips: Know if your home is near a creek that floods.
Trim limbs over the roof before storm season.
Add a vapor barrier and keep crawl space vents working.
Have a plan and a safe room for tornado warnings.
areas: Calls come from Five Points, Twickenham, Old Town, Blossomwood, Jones Valley, Hampton Cove, Monte Sano and Edgewater, plus Madison, Harvest and Meridianville.

faq.q: Does my Huntsville home policy cover creek flooding?
faq.a: No. Only a flood policy covers water that rises from a creek or runs in over the ground. A home policy covers sudden leaks and storm damage that opens the roof. NFIP policies usually take 30 days to start, so buy one before storm season.
